seo.title: Best Cheap Eats in Casablanca (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Casablanca's top 12 cheap eats, from authentic Moroccan tagines to savory street food. Find budget-friendly restaurants and local favorites for under $10-15 per person.

hero.subtitle: Explore the vibrant culinary scene of Casablanca without breaking the bank. Our curated list highlights local favorites, hidden gems, and must-try street food for every budget traveler.

picks.name: Chez Madame Salma
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A beloved local institution, Chez Madame Salma offers authentic Moroccan home cooking in a no-frills setting. Known for its generous portions and flavors that taste just like grandma made them, it's a staple for a truly local culinary experience without tourist pricing.
picks.whatToOrder: Tagine de poulet aux citrons confits (Chicken tagine with preserved lemons)
picks.insiderTip: Go early for lunch as it gets very crowded with local office workers. Be prepared for a bustling, lively atmosphere.
picks.redditQuote: "Chez Madame Salma is legit. Don't expect fancy, just expect amazing food. Their tagines are insane and so cheap. Worth the hunt!"

picks.name: Snack Amine
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A highly popular spot for quick, delicious, and incredibly affordable sandwiches, paninis, and wraps. Snack Amine is a bustling eatery frequented by locals for its fresh ingredients, speedy service, and satisfying portions, making it perfect for a grab-and-go lunch.
picks.whatToOrder: Sandwich Mixte (mixed meats and salads in baguette)
picks.insiderTip: Their harissa (spicy sauce) is homemade and famous; ask for it on the side if you like a kick!
picks.redditQuote: "Snack Amine is my go-to for a quick, cheap bite in Habous. That 'Mixte' sandwich hits different every time, and the price is unbeatable."

picks.name: Dar Naji
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While slightly more upscale in ambiance than some cheap eats, Dar Naji offers excellent value for traditional Moroccan cuisine, especially their seafood dishes. The elegant decor provides a pleasant dining experience without a hefty price tag, making it ideal for a relaxed meal.
picks.insiderTip: Their fresh juice selection is fantastic and pairs perfectly with the rich Moroccan dishes.
picks.redditQuote: "Dar Naji is a great balance of traditional Moroccan food, nice atmosphere, and not too expensive. The fish pastilla there is a must-try."

picks.name: Restaurant Loubane
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Restaurant Loubane brings a fresh, slightly more modern approach to traditional Moroccan cuisine, often focusing on lighter, healthier preparations. It's a favorite among younger locals and those seeking quality food made with fresh ingredients in a stylish, yet unpretentious, setting.
picks.insiderTip: They have great fresh salads and smoothies, perfect if you're looking for something lighter.
picks.redditQuote: "Loubane in Gauthier is my favorite for a healthier, modern Moroccan meal that still feels authentic. Their veggie tagine is surprisingly good."

picks.name: Pâtisserie Bennis Habous
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A legendary patisserie in the charming Habous district, Bennis is famous for its exquisite traditional Moroccan pastries. While not a full meal spot, it's an essential cheap eat experience for indulging in sweet treats and strong Moroccan mint tea amidst the bustling souk atmosphere.
picks.whatToOrder: Cornes de gazelle (Gazelle horns) and a glass of Atay (Mint Tea)
picks.insiderTip: Buy a selection of small pastries by weight to try a variety. They make great gifts too!
picks.redditQuote: "You CANNOT go to Habous without stopping at Pâtisserie Bennis. Their cornes de gazelle are pure magic, and it's so cheap for such quality."

picks.name: Habous Food Stalls (Collective)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The vibrant food stalls scattered throughout the Habous district offer an immersive culinary adventure. Here, you can sample a wide array of authentic Moroccan street food, from savory brochettes and kefta to various types of bread and local snacks, all prepared fresh before your eyes.
picks.whatToOrder: Brochettes (skewers) of chicken or kefta (minced meat), with fresh bread.
picks.insiderTip: Don't be afraid to try different stalls. Look for the ones with the most locals for the best and freshest options.
picks.redditQuote: "Just wander through Habous and pick a food stall that looks busy. The brochettes are usually fire and super cheap. Best way to eat local."

picks.name: Restaurant Châab
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Restaurant Châab is a no-frills, authentic Moroccan eatery popular with locals for its hearty portions and simple, delicious home-style cooking. It's particularly known for its grilled meats and traditional stews, offering a genuine taste of Moroccan comfort food in a relaxed setting.
picks.whatToOrder: Couscous (especially on Fridays, the traditional day for it)
picks.insiderTip: Portions are generous, so consider sharing if you're not super hungry.
picks.redditQuote: "Châab is a classic. Nothing fancy, but their couscous is proper, and you won't leave hungry. It's a real local spot, which I love."

picks.name: Snack Ali Baba
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Another favorite among Casablanca's fast-casual scene, Snack Ali Baba is renowned for its delicious grilled sandwiches, juicy burgers, and a variety of quick Moroccan-inspired bites. It's a lively spot perfect for a speedy and satisfying meal that won't strain your wallet.
picks.whatToOrder: Panini au poulet (Chicken Panini) or their famous Kefta Sandwich.
picks.insiderTip: Their fresh orange juice is a fantastic addition to any meal here.
picks.redditQuote: "Ali Baba's kefta sandwich is a lifesaver when you need something quick and tasty. So much flavor for just a few dirhams."

picks.name: Mahrajane
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Mahrajane is a long-standing Casablanca institution offering a wide array of classic Moroccan dishes in a welcoming, traditional setting. Known for its consistent quality and generous portions, it’s an excellent choice for experiencing authentic Moroccan flavors at a very reasonable price point.
picks.whatToOrder: Tanjia Marrakchia (slow-cooked lamb or beef) or a mixed grill platter.
picks.insiderTip: Ask for their daily specials – often they have unique regional dishes not on the regular menu.
picks.redditQuote: "Mahrajane is solid for classic Moroccan. The Tanjia is really good, and it feels like a proper meal, not just a quick snack. Great value."

picks.name: Restaurant El Mida
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located near the bustling fish market, Restaurant El Mida offers incredibly fresh seafood at unbeatable prices. You can often choose your fish directly from the day's catch, which is then grilled or fried to perfection. It's a rustic, authentic experience for seafood lovers.
picks.whatToOrder: Grilled whole fish (e.g., Daurade or Sardines) with a side of Moroccan salad.
picks.insiderTip: The prices for fish are typically by weight. Don't be shy to ask for the price before they cook it.
picks.redditQuote: "If you love seafood and want it fresh and cheap, El Mida by Casa Port is the spot. Pick your own fish, get it grilled, simple perfection."

picks.name: Boulangerie Pâtisserie Al Baraka
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Al Baraka is a widespread and popular chain of bakeries and patisseries across Casablanca, offering a huge selection of fresh breads, viennoiseries, traditional Moroccan pastries, and light snacks. It’s an ideal spot for a quick, affordable breakfast or a coffee break.
picks.whatToOrder: Moroccan msemen (flatbread) with honey and a fresh orange juice, or a croissant.
picks.insiderTip: Many locations have a small café area where you can sit and enjoy your purchases with a hot drink.
picks.redditQuote: "Al Baraka is my morning ritual. Fresh msemen and coffee for practically nothing. Can't beat it for a cheap, authentic breakfast."

picks.name: La Grillardière
picks.whyItMadeTheList: La Grillardière is a local favorite renowned for its succulent grilled meats and simple, hearty Moroccan fare. Specializing in brochettes, kefta, and various cuts of grilled chicken and beef, it offers a satisfying meal in a casual, family-friendly atmosphere at a great price.
picks.whatToOrder: Brochettes mixtes (mixed skewers) with fries and Moroccan salad.
picks.insiderTip: It can get quite busy, especially on weekend evenings, so arrive a bit earlier if you prefer a quieter experience.
picks.redditQuote: "For proper grilled meat, La Grillardière is the place. Their mixed skewers are fantastic and a solid portion for the price. Always a good choice."

faq.question: Is it safe to eat street food in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Generally, yes, but exercise common sense. Look for stalls with high customer turnover, fresh ingredients visible, and clean preparation areas. If food is cooked to order and served hot, it's usually a safer bet. Trust your instincts and observe where locals are eating.

faq.question: What's a typical price for a cheap meal in Casablanca?
faq.answer: You can easily find a satisfying and delicious meal for anywhere between 30-80 MAD (approximately $3-8 USD) per person at local snack places, street food stalls, or simple traditional restaurants. For a full sit-down meal, expect to pay closer to 60-100 MAD ($6-10 USD).

faq.question: Are vegetarian cheap eats easy to find in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Yes, Morocco is very vegetarian-friendly. Many traditional dishes like vegetable tagines, couscous with seven vegetables, lentil soup (harira), and various salads are widely available and often very affordable. Simply ask for 'sans viande' (without meat).

faq.question: Do I need to tip at cheap eat places in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Tipping is appreciated but not strictly mandatory at very casual or street food spots. For small restaurants, leaving a few dirhams (5-10 MAD) is a nice gesture if service was good. For larger bills, rounding up or adding 5-10% is customary.

faq.question: What are common cheap breakfast options in Casablanca?
faq.answer: For a cheap and authentic Moroccan breakfast, head to local bakeries or cafes. You'll find fresh bread (khobz), msemen (pan-fried flatbread), baghrir (pancakes) with honey and butter, olives, cheese, and a glass of mint tea or coffee for a few dirhams.

faq.question: Are food delivery apps available for cheap eats in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Yes, popular food delivery apps like Glovo and Jumia Food operate in Casablanca and often feature many of the city's affordable eateries. This can be a convenient option if you prefer to eat in or are staying in an area further from the listed venues.

methodology: Our selection of Casablanca's best cheap eats is based on extensive local research, diner reviews, and expert recommendations, focusing on venues offering exceptional value, authentic flavors, and a memorable experience. We prioritized establishments where a satisfying meal can be enjoyed for under 100 MAD (approximately $10-15 USD) per person, without compromising on quality or atmosphere.
